fullPassage:
Every language has its distinctive expressions, but some places have truly unique and culturally rich idioms and sayings. Ready to explore some of the most unique idioms from around the world? Join us on a journey to discover them!
When your German friend says "Have a pig!" to you, it's a way of wishing you good luck. The saying dates back to medieval times when farmers who could raise many pigs were considered prosperous. Therefore, as New Year's Eve approaches, people in Germany give each other candies in a pig shape as a way to wish each other good luck in the coming year.
In Thailand, when people say "You're riding an elephant to catch a grasshopper," they mean that you're putting in a tremendous amount of effort for a very small reward. It's quite simple to understand. Imagine trying to catch a tiny grasshopper by riding a massive elephant — it's a huge effort for a tiny result.
In Portugal, there's a saying: "Don't feed the donkey sponge cake." This expression emphasizes the idea of not giving valuable things to those who don't appreciate or deserve them. It's pretty simple — donkeys are perfectly happy with carrots and sugar, so there's no need to give them your sponge cake!
In Finland, if you say the wrong thing, you're "letting a frog out of your mouth"! That makes sense since spitting a frog at someone is generally a bad idea. Finland is considered one of the greenest countries on earth, so it should be no surprise that the Finns enjoy nature idioms.
